text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- A proposal from European Parliament member Lone Dybkjaer for making English the EU working language and foregoing Denmarks's right to appoint a commissioner has brought strong criticism at home and calls for foreign minister Niels Helveg Petersen to call Dybkjaer to call her to order.

--- Postal distribution in Denmark has improved after postmen's working hours were changed from piece-work to a common 37 hour work week. The aim is now to deleiver 97 percent of post the day after it is posted.
--- Denmark is to have a national strategy to prevent suicides and health authorities have formed a working group which is to draft policy in cooperation with local authorities and hospitals.

--- Telecommunication company Tele Danmark has now moved from number three to four on the OECD ranking list of the cheapest telecom service countries in the world including both private and business customers.
--- Both Spain and Germany are now seeking EU state subsidies for ailing ship yards. These subsidies could be used for price dumping, creating even more difficulties for troubled Danish shipyeards.
